look_here_first: Inspect the tiny bract halfway along each flower stalk (pedicel), then the short raceme peduncle and flower center. Five sterile stamens (staminodes) help separate this species from bractless Samolus ebracteatus. A leaf rosette alone cannot settle the identification.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Minute bract at the midpoint of each flower pedicel.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Racemose inflorescence with peduncle to 0.7 cm.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Five fertile stamens opposite the corolla lobes and five staminodes.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Small corolla, 1.2–3 mm long; mature capsules 2–3 mm.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Light-green herbaceous perennial, about 0.7–8.2 dm tall in FNA; stems erect or ascending.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Simple, alternate; basal and stem leaves or all stem leaves. Blades obovate, broadly spatulate to elliptic, 1.5–15 cm, with rounded to obtuse tips.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Usually racemose, terminal or terminal and axillary, with short peduncle to 0.7 cm; pedicels 1.5–14 mm and bracteate at midlength.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Corolla 1.2–3 mm long with five lobes; five fertile stamens opposite lobes, plus five staminodes.

key_traits.label: Lookalike separators
key_traits.text: Samolus ebracteatus: no pedicel bracts, longer peduncle about 5–10 cm, no staminodes, and larger corolla (3–7.5 mm). Do not use flower color, moist habitat, or leaf rosette alone. Broad Samolus valerandi is an alternative taxonomic treatment; only subsp. parviflorus is mapped here.
